Settings ported from HTTP/2 might","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":12,"modality":0,"text":"choose to redeﬁne their value to limit it to 30 bits for more eﬃcient encoding or to make use of","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":13,"modality":0,"text":"the 62-bit space ifmore than 30 bits are required.","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":14,"modality":0,"text":"Settings need to be deﬁned separately for HTTP/2 and HTTP/3. See Section 7.2.4.2.","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":20,"modality":0,"text":"A.4. However,","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":22,"modality":0,"text":"the diﬀerences between HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 mean that error codes are not directly portable","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":23,"modality":0,"text":"between versions.","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":24,"modality":0,"text":"The HTTP/2 error codes deﬁned in Section 7 of [HTTP/2] logically map to the HTTP/3 error codes","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":25,"modality":0,"text":"as follows:","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":26,"modality":0,"text":"NO_ERROR (0x00): H3_NO_ERROR in Section 8.1.","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":27,"modality":0,"text":"PROTOCOL_ERROR (0x01): This is mapped to H3_GENERAL_PROTOCOL_ERROR except in cases","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":28,"modality":0,"text":"where more speciﬁc error codes have been deﬁned. Mappingbetween HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 Errors","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":57,"modality":0,"text":"An intermediary that converts between HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 may encounter error conditions","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":58,"modality":0,"text":"from either upstream. It is useful to communicate the occurrence of errors to the downstream,","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":59,"modality":0,"text":"but error codes largely reﬂect connection-local problems that generally do not make sense to","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":60,"modality":0,"text":"propagate.","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":61,"modality":0,"text":"An intermediary that encounters an error from an upstream origin can indicate this by sending","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":62,"modality":0,"text":"an HTTP status code such as 502 (Bad Gateway), which is suitable for a broad class of errors.","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":63,"modality":0,"text":"There are some rare cases where it is beneﬁcial to propagate the error by mapping it to the closest","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":64,"modality":0,"text":"matching error type to the receiver. For example, an intermediary that receives an HTTP/2","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":65,"modality":0,"text":"stream error oftype REFUSED_STREAM from the origin has a clear signal that the request was not","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":66,"modality":0,"text":"processed and that the request is safe to retry. Propagating this error condition to the client as an","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":67,"modality":0,"text":"HTTP/3 stream error oftype H3_REQUEST_REJECTED allows the client to take the action it deems","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":68,"modality":0,"text":"most appropriate.
